points.label: Property overview
points.description: Start with the property at the center of the aerial view.

quiz.question: Before planning work from an aerial image, how should you confirm the area you are assessing?
options: Assume the image edges show the legal property boundary.
Confirm the property location and boundaries using verified site information.
Treat every nearby building as part of the same property.

points.explanation: The image is centered on address coordinates. Its edges and the checkpoint markers do not define property boundaries.

points.label: Access review
points.description: Use the surrounding imagery to begin reviewing possible site access.

quiz.question: What is the best next step when a route in the aerial image appears to lead onto the site?
options: Confirm the entrance, permissions, and current route conditions with site information.
Assume the route is open because it is visible.
Choose the shortest route without checking restrictions.

points.explanation: Aerial imagery can suggest a route, but it does not establish that an entrance is open, permitted, or suitable today.

points.label: Surroundings review
points.description: Zoom out to review how the property relates to its surroundings.

quiz.question: Why review a wider aerial view before planning activity at the property?
options: It replaces checking current conditions on site.
It proves every visible area is available for storage.
It helps identify nearby roads, buildings, and other areas that need further review.

points.explanation: A wider view provides context for planning. Follow up on visible features with current, verified site information.
